title: Canon PowerShot V1 Vlog Camera [AU Version] $888 (RRP $1,449) Delivered @ Amazon AU
body:
Deal: Canon PowerShot V1 Vlog Camera [AU Version] $888 (RRP $1,449) Delivered @ Amazon AU

[Tanvry] For vlogging won't a dji pocket be better
[artcvan] I'd say it depends on the person and the type of vlogging they want to do. For 95% of people an Osmo Pocket is probably easier. But if you want to be a bit more versatile and have better quality, a G7X/RX100/ZV-1 is where you want to be, since they can be used as a regular point and shoot as well.
Also much larger viewfinder on point and shoots which arguably would be better for vlogging
[Skinnerr] The price is reflected in the rx100 being double this as it's a pocket zoom lens and makeshift all in one camera.
[Jimothy Wongingtons] Osmo 3 is actually pog af - quite fun can recommend
[AustAust] Definitely, it's part of why this camera is so heavily discounted - the V nomenclature is an albatross for sales now the Pocket 3, 4, 4p, Insta360 Luna, etc exist.
This is a wayyyyyyy better stills camera, and significantly outperforms the much more expensive G7xiii. Just putting a flash on it is really annoying.
[Tanvry] yeah stills for sure, but for vlogs it's not going to be as stable as one with a gimbal
[Hugh G Rection] any can work really. but this is better than the dji because it has real optical zoom, a larger sensor for richer depth-of-field, and a setup better suited for stationary talking-head videos and way better photos.
[Tanvry] dji pocket also has real x3 optical zoom though
[mattman] Compared to DJI pocket:
Better photo capabilities
Real optical zoom, not digital (albeit limited)
Swappable batteries
Much longer continuous record time via inbuilt fan
DJI really only workable with DJI mics, this has 3.5mm line for any mic
Compared to g7x:
Fat
Less zoom
Better wide angle
NO BUILT IN FLASH
Pocket still better for that "walking around" video
G7x better for stills where zoom/flash needed & video less important
These a pretty decent in the middle somewhere, depending on needs.
[Dandaman21] Good info! I'm basically replacing my phone camera, decided the discount compared to the G7x and actually being able to get one was worth it.
[AustAust] The V1 has a significantly larger sensor than the g7xiii, with significantly newer tech in it - the g7xiii is smaller, but it's so much more expensive that the V1 is just a better option.
Putting a flash on the V1 is really annoying though because of the canon multi function shoe nonsense.
[chuie] Image quality will be "better" but if just for vlogging/social media you'd have to weigh up the extra step in processing compared to smartphone.
Also will probably be disappointing in low-light with a 1-inchish sensor.
Personally I'd go at least micro 4-3rds/APS-C for a compact camera since the image quality/low-light gathering jump is enough to justify using over smartphone. But that also comes with price and size (Fujifilm x100vi, Lumix L10, and you have money to burn Sony RX1riii/Leica etc).
[Bacons] powershot v1 sensor is smidge larger than a m43
[Thayer] The V1 is f/2.8 wide and f/4.5 tele, an MFT f/1.4 lens is 2 stops (4×) brighter at the wide end, and ~3 stops (~10×) brighter at the tele end.
Even at the same sensor size, MFT with a fast lens gives a significant low-light advantage.
[mattman] Where is this mythical 12-25 F1.4 MFT lens that fits in your pocket and is available with a body for sub $1k total?
[Thayer] @mattman: OP noted it "comes with price and size"
It is worth mentioning there's still a low-light advantage with MFT and a fast lens, even at the same sensor size.
Different trade-offs, up to what you prioritise.
There are also plenty of good value compact MFT bodies that pair well with cheap f/1.7-1.8 primes for a solid low-light setup.
Coming from someone who's grappled with MFT low-light. Worth setting realistic expectations on what the system can and can't do.
[ahboy] @mattman: Always bothers me people who complain about this range/aperture when the MFT lens with this range is constant f4.0, weighs as much as the V1 by itself and costs about 15% more on top!
[ahboy] @Thayer: It seemed like a common comment when the product was announced as people would cite the ZV-1's non vlog friendly zoom being f1.8-2.8 as the expectation, even though the ZV-1M2 was already out with 18-50mm f1.8-4 (on a smaller sensor) and no OIS.
Most critical reviews also mention it and I thought it was just rather unfair all things considered when I checked out equivalent MFT lenses.
[dukeGR4] they should launch a photo-centric version, would sell like hot cakes. maybe give it EV.
[mindlessshopper] Was just thinking about getting dji pocket 3 and this come up !
[tossmysaladandeggs] I'm thinking of buying a camera for when I travel and I'd love something that can capture natural landscapes far better than a phone camera. Would the V1 be the right sort of camera for better quality images? I would strictly only use it for travel photos
[ahboy] James Reader who is a Canon user has reviewed the camera and you can get an idea of the footage and shots he gets from it:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2mHzUoyORho
There's quite a few reviews on YouTube on the camera, including some long term reviews which seem pretty positive along with the comments.
Edit:
Should note that despite the camera being quite capable for stills, it's not exactly convenient to share/upload photos from it immediately like it would be on a smartphone.
